title: Ibn al-Haytham: the scientist who explained how we see

figure.name: x-compare
figure.verdict: Test ideas, do not just trust them

explain.say: Here is a question that puzzled people for thousands of years: when you look at a tree, does something go out of your eyes, or come into them? Look at the two ideas on the board.

draw.text: Ibn al-Haytham: the scientist who explained how we see

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Test ideas, do not just trust them

explain.say: On the left is the old idea. Famous Greek thinkers taught that eyes shoot out rays, like torches, that touch what we see. People believed it for over a thousand years. Does that sound right to you?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Test ideas, do not just trust them

explain.say: About 1,000 years ago, a scientist named Ibn al-Haytham, born in Basra in Iraq and working in Cairo, said no. Look at the right: light bounces off the tree and travels in straight lines into your eye. Can you see the last point?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Test ideas, do not just trust them

explain.say: Proved by experiments! He tested his ideas instead of just trusting old books. Look at his famous test with a dark room and a tiny hole, called a camera obscura.

faq.a: Ibn al-Haytham, known in Europe as Alhazen, was a scientist born in Basra, Iraq, around 965 CE, who worked in Cairo. His Book of Optics explained light and vision using experiments.
Light from a lamp or the Sun bounces off objects and travels in straight lines into our eyes. The eye focuses it, and the brain makes a picture.
Camera obscura means dark room. Light from outside passes through a tiny hole and makes an upside-down picture on the opposite wall.
asks: Why is the picture upside down?

faq.q: What is the Book of Optics?
faq.a: A seven-volume book Ibn al-Haytham wrote between about 1011 and 1021. It was translated into Latin and studied by European scientists for centuries.

faq.q: Why is Ibn al-Haytham called an early scientist?
faq.a: He insisted on checking ideas with careful experiments and measurements, not just trusting famous authors. That is the core of the scientific method.
asks: Did Ibn al-Haytham invent the scientific method?

facts: Ibn al-Haytham wrote his Book of Optics between about 1011 and 1021 CE.
He showed that vision happens when light enters the eye, not when the eye sends out rays.

quiz.say: Why is the picture in a camera obscura upside down?
quiz.show: Why is the picture in a camera obscura upside down?

options.show: Light travels in straight lines and crosses at the hole
options.say: Light travels in straight lines and crosses at the hole

quiz.why: Rays from the top of the scene go down through the hole and rays from the bottom go up, so the picture flips.

wrong.1: A flat wall still shows the flipped picture.
wrong.2: The darkness helps you see the picture; it does not flip it.
